raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, and on 5 mu I can’t gamble too much. Same as most years, I’ll keep the wheat-maize rotation. Wheat and maize together are steady for us. If one side is not so good, the other can still help. I only finished primary school, so I don’t calculate like technicians do. I look at what happened before, what the neighbors are doing, and whether I have enough cash in hand. Last year the wheat did decent with moderate fertilizer and three irrigations, and the maize was alright with one watering after sowing and another if the summer turns dry. Fertilizer is expensive, so I won’t push too hard, but I also don’t dare cut too much because if the crop turns yellow, yield drops fast. Family labor is limited because some people work outside, so I keep things simple and do what fits our hands and timing, especially the few days between wheat harvest and maize sowing.
